searchText: Why don't we increase the `MIN_SYNC_COMMITTEE_PARTICIPANTS` to a reasonable number such that this kind of attack requires a larger stake? If I understand your reasoning correctly, you rely on: - an entity having a validator in the sync committee - said entity being able to eclipse a particular light client By that logic, increasing `MIN_SYNC_COMMITTEE_PARTICIPANTS` would only make the problem worse no? Increasing `MIN_SYNC_COMMITTEE_PARTICIPANTS` would imply you would need more more participants in the sync committee consider an update valid? As per my understanding that should help It is up to the use case and the client implementation to determine what risk profile to apply. The standard "safe" mechanism is using 2/3 majority, as well as requires a `finality_proof`. This is the behaviour you get if you just never call `process_slot_for_light_client_store`. Anything else is heuristics based. The only time when you can _realistically_ get stuck following that, is: – no finality for an entire sync committee period – low sync committee participation (< 2/3) for an entire sync committee period If your use case cannot fallback to an alternate syncing mechanism to cover such edge case periods, you need a heuristic to avoid getting stuck.

excerpts.author: etan_status
excerpts.content:
It is up to the use case and the client implementation to determine what risk profile to apply. 
The standard "safe" mechanism is using 2/3 majority, as well as requires a `finality_proof`. 
This is the behaviour you get if you just never call `process_slot_for_light_client_store`. Anything else is heuristics based.

The only time when you can _realistically_ get stuck following that, is:
– no finality for an entire sync committee period
– low sync committee participation (< 2/3) for an entire sync committee period
If your use case cannot fallback to an alternate syncing mechanism to cover such edge case periods, you need a heuristic to avoid getting stuck.
